answer: Clique-Density Entry Pricing. Each agent may harbor at most k inbound trust links per 30-day window; the admission price for a new identity scales with the local edge density of its introducers' neighborhood. Dense clusters (suspected copies) pay exponentially more to enter, while sparse regions stay cheap. The ledger keeps a rolling vault of per-node link schedules so wash cycles cannot reset the counter. Attackers must mirror a genuine sparse topology before every registration: splitting farms, aging links, and paying latency.
